apps.name: CrowdSec
apps.tagline: Detect and block malicious IPs automatically
apps.description: Watches your logs for brute-force attempts, scans and known attack patterns, and blocks the offending IPs — sharing (and benefiting from) threat intelligence across the whole CrowdSec community. It needs your own log files and a bouncer (like the MikroTik one below) to actually act on what it finds.
apps.first_run: CrowdSec has no browser dashboard. Open a Terminal and run "docker exec -it <container> cscli bouncers add my-bouncer" to get an API key for a bouncer, and "cscli decisions list" to see what it has blocked.

releases.notes: Added to the NoCapOS App Store.

apps.name: CrowdSec MikroTik Bouncer
apps.tagline: Enforce CrowdSec bans on a MikroTik router
apps.description: Applies CrowdSec's ban decisions directly to a MikroTik RouterOS router's address lists and firewall rules, blocking malicious IPs at the network edge.
apps.first_run: This does nothing until you edit its environment in Containers and fill in CROWDSEC_URL, CROWDSEC_BOUNCER_API_KEY (from "cscli bouncers add" on the CrowdSec app), MIKROTIK_HOST, MIKROTIK_USER and MIKROTIK_PASS, then restart it. It has no browser dashboard.

releases.notes: Added to the NoCapOS App Store.

apps.name: Fail2ban
apps.tagline: Ban IPs after repeated failed logins
apps.description: Watches logs for repeated failed sign-in attempts — SSH, web logins and more — and bans the offending IPs with the host firewall. In container form it needs your own log files and host-level network access to actually enforce bans; expect to edit its volumes and capabilities by hand after install.
apps.first_run: This needs your log files bind-mounted in and NET_ADMIN plus host networking added under its container settings before bans actually take effect. It has no browser dashboard.
